Problem.description:
An RFC 9457 problem document. Every refusal this platform writes has this shape, on `application/problem+json`.

RFC 9457 permits extension members and this platform uses one, `code`. Switch on that rather than on `type`: a URI invites prefix-matching and string surgery, and the short token is the thing that stays readable in a client.

code.description: The extension member a client switches on, e.g. `PLAYBACK_NOT_ENTITLED`. Absent when the refusal has no machine-readable identity behind it, such as a bare `ResponseStatusException`.

detail.description: What went wrong THIS time, written for whoever is on the other end. Absent when the refusal must not describe itself.

instance.description: The occurrence this document is about, when there is one.

status.description: The HTTP status code, repeated in the document.

title.description: A short, human-readable summary of the kind of problem.

type.description: A stable URI identifying the kind of problem. It does not resolve; RFC 9457 says it need not.
